title: Smoothness of a quotient by quadratic relations at an annihilator-good prime
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, with S a Noetherian R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let π∈R, K⊆S an ideal with K⊆(π²) and (π)K⊆K², and q∈Spec(S/K). Suppose π∈q. Put p=q∩S. Assume R→S is smooth at p [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and S_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat over R [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. If r∈R has rπx=0 whenever π²x=0 in R, and the image of r is outside q, then R→S/K is smooth at q. This statement has no input algebra A, section modulo π⁴, strictly standard hypothesis, or global singular-ideal conclusion.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Set p=q∩S, T=S_p, J=KT, and t=image of π in T. Localization carries the two ideal containments to J⊆(t²) and (t)J⊆J². T is Noetherian and local and t belongs to its maximal ideal. Thus N=(t)J satisfies N⊆J²⊆(t²)J=(t)N. N is finitely generated, and (t) is contained in the Jacobson radical. Apply Nakayama to obtain N=0.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Flat base change of annihilators gives Ann_T(t²)=Ann_R(π²)T. For each generator x in Ann_R(π²), the assumption on r gives rπx=0; induction over the ideal span proves image(r)t z=0 for every z∈Ann_T(t²). Since image(r) is a unit in T, tz=0. Hence Ann_T(t²)=Ann_T(t). If x∈J, write x=t²z. As (t)J=0, t³z=0. Apply annihilator stability first to tz, giving t²z=0 (equivalently apply it twice to obtain tz=0). Thus x=0 and J=0.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators of K. Since their images vanish in S_p, each is killed by some denominator outside p. The product s of these denominators is outside p and kills every generator, hence all of K, by linearity. The empty generating set uses s=1.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Choose g outside p whose principal localization S_g is smooth. Put e=sg. Localize S_g further at s, and identify this iterated localization with S_e; smooth composition shows S_e is smooth. The canonical localization map S_e→(S/K)_e is surjective. Its injectivity criterion says every x∈K must be killed by a power of e; the first power works since sK=0. Therefore this map is an R-algebra isomorphism and (S/K)_e is smooth. The image of e lies outside q, proving smoothness at q.
